LESSON: INTERPERSONAL ENVIRONMENT

Grade: PP1
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: SOCIAL
Topic 1.4: Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT from Kenya
3. practise Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT in clear steps
4. apply Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INTERPERSONAL ENVIRONMENT
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: INTERPERSONAL ENVIRONMENT
Study Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT from Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT from Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT in clear steps. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT in clear steps.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT in one real-life situation this week.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT” around your school. (skill: explain what Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Say why Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT from Kenya)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT this week. (skill: practise Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT in clear steps)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT” around your school. (skill: apply Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.
